chunks: He (peace be upon him) said: Indeed, Allah, the Exalted, is not unjust to His servants. He is more Knowing of what is in the breasts, more Seeing of what is in the eyes, and closer than the jugular vein. Nothing hidden escapes Him, nothing absent is lost to Him, no deed is wasted with Him, no good deed is missed by Him, and no bad deed is lost with Him. All are with Him in their measure. He is the All-Forgiving, the Merciful, the Loving, the Glorious, the Lord of the Glorious Throne. He does what He wills. He is not questioned about what He does, but they are questioned. To Him belongs the command, and to Him the matter is returned. Indeed, for Him is creation and command. Blessed is Allah, Lord of the worlds.

key_terms.ذُو الْعَرْشِ الْمَجِيدُ: The Lord of the Glorious Throne
key_terms.لَا يُسْأَلُ عَمَّا يَفْعَلُ: Not questioned about what He does

ai.seo_question: What does this hadith say about Allah's justice and knowledge of deeds?
ai.summary: In *Kamal al-Din*, Shaykh al-Saduq utilizes this narration to reinforce the doctrine of *Adl* (Divine Justice) as a fundamental pillar of Shia theology, countering the Mu'tazila and Ash'ari debates on whether God is bound by justice. The text underscores that Allah’s justice is intrinsic to His nature, ensuring that every atom of good or evil is meticulously accounted for in the divine record, thereby affirming human accountability without implying compulsion.
